newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices fall on low consumer buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices fall on low consumer buying.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Wednesday fell on low consumer buying and profit-taking by stockists trimming recent gains, dealers said.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 fell by 10 rupees at 1,290/1,340 rupees per quintal while M-30 moved down by 20 rupees at 1,340/1,380 rupees.
"Trading volume was at a low ebb due to the absence of any arrivals from mills to the market following the strike by the transport operators," one dealer said.
"Even the offtake of sugar also remained low as no trucks were available to deliver sugar from the wholesale market to retail counters," he said.
"Some of the retail counters in the Bombay city are now facing shortage and prices at the retail centres counters may move up if the strike continues," he added.
